findings.atomic_item: find whether there is a stronger paper in this data that is not being written — something unexplored, or explored but under-executed or under-explained
findings.location: Deliverable (iii) Scope of Novelty, Ranked — '### B. The ranked list' (line 271 onward). The word 'UNEXPLORED' appears zero times in the entire report; grep confirms 0 hits.
findings.issue: The query names FOUR novelty categories and the decomposition carries entity 'the unexplored paper' (required_fields: 'result the data would support but the paper does not attempt', 'motivating literature', 'tag') plus sub-question 23 ('Is there a stronger paper here that is entirely UNEXPLORED — a result the data would support that the paper does not attempt at all, distinct from results it explored but under-executed or under-explained?'); the draft labels only UNDER-STATED (RANK 3) and UNDER-EXECUTED (RANK 9), and never designates any item as unexplored.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly designate at least one ranked item as the UNEXPLORED finding and label it as such. RANK 6's landscape-covariate negative and its cross-sectional 'multiplicative mechanism' statement (Spearman 0.84-0.96 rank stability against magnitude collapse to ~0.01 under perturbation) is the strongest candidate already in the draft — it is an analysis the paper does not attempt at all, motivated by the ELA literature [67][68][69][71]. Add a one-clause category label ('UNEXPLORED — the paper does not attempt this analysis at all') to that item's header and state in '### B' preamble which rank numbers map to which of the four categories, so the four are distinguishable at a glance. Keep the existing FOLD-INTO-THIS-PAPER / CHEAP tag.
findings.priority_note: This is the category the step-1 coverage audit already caught being dropped once. It is now dropped again in the final draft.

findings.recommendation: Two surgical moves. (1) Label RANK 8 explicitly as the UNDER-EXPLAINED finding — append 'The clearest under-explained finding' to its header, mirroring RANK 3's existing 'The clearest under-stated finding' phrasing. (2) Add a short RANK 8a (or fold into RANK 8) giving frozen cells / LCB paralysis its sharper frame: the report already has the material in (i.B) — Yarotsky (2013) Theorem 3, EI-driven BO started at the optimum converging back to it and 'not dense' [24], plus Ament et al.'s numerical vanishing-gradient pathology [87] and Kim & Choi on local-versus-global acquisition optimizers [25].
